title: One million contributors. Building what comes next.
summary: One million people in 175+ countries have signed up to contribute to Luel. Why that reach matters for frontier labs building multimodal AI, for our own research and for the people behind the data.
body_markdown:
For everyone who has shared their voice, recorded a conversation, filmed a task or lent their expertise: thank you. Your work goes into the datasets we deliver to AI labs, the models we build and the research we do at[Luel Labs](https://www.luel.ai/lab) .


## The data the next models need


The open web has given models most of what it can. The data the next systems need was never posted online: conversations in regional speech, first-person video of everyday tasks, people talking and working in real rooms, on real phones, on noisy streets. Someone has to record it, on purpose.


Many gaps in AI start as gaps in data. A language can have millions of speakers and almost no recordings a model can learn from. A household task looks different in every home, while the datasets used to learn it show only a few of them.


## Range, not volume


For a multimodal model, hours of data matter less than how many different people, places and conditions are in it. A model trained on a hundred speakers learns those voices. One trained on thousands starts to learn the language. Video works the same way: more homes, more hands, more tools, more kinds of light.


A million contributors gives us that range. We can reach a specific community, add more independent speakers, or record in the rooms and on the phones people really use. More speakers of one language bring the regional accents that were missing. More places bring conditions a model has never seen. That is what decides whether a model works outside the settings it was built in.


## What it means for frontier labs


The teams building multimodal AI rarely need more data in general. They need a specific slice: one dialect, one task filmed from the wearer's point of view, one kind of call. A larger network lets us collect that slice to a written spec, deeper within one community or across many languages and environments at once.


It also makes the second collection possible. When an evaluation finds a gap, a lab can ask for exactly the speakers, settings or actions that were missing, and we can reach the people who have them. Test sets can come from different people than the training data, so a score reflects people the model has never heard or seen.


Reach alone is not enough, so our quality work grows with it: quality assurance, fraud detection, filtering, labeling and cleaning. The models we build for that work are what turn real-world recordings into data a team can train on. And the data arrives rights-cleared, so it can pass procurement as well as evaluation.


## The network and the lab feed each other


When useful data is scarce, access to the right people decides whether a research project is practical at all. Native speakers in the network made our voices in[Dzongkha](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/dzongkha-emotive-tts) ,[Moroccan Darija](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/moroccan-darija-tts) ,[Tibetan](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/lhasa-tibetan-tts) and[Egyptian Arabic](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/masri-egyptian-tts) possible. Real conversations recorded by contributors trained[Multi-Speaker Separation](https://www.luel.ai/blog/luel-multi-speaker-separation) . Calls from people held out of training are how we tested[Accentus](https://www.luel.ai/blog/accentus-american-accent-detection) .


The loop we run for labs runs inside our own research too. When one of our models struggles with an accent or a noisy room, the next collection targets exactly that. A million contributors means we can take on more of those questions, in more languages and more modalities.


## A direct way to take part


Our contributors choose what they share, consent to how it is used and are paid for every accepted submission. For people whose languages and daily lives are missing from AI, that is a direct way to help shape it.


One million signups does not close every gap. It gives us a larger base to find them and fill them, with the people who know them best.


## What comes next


Next, we put that reach to work. We will add more languages, collect in more real-world settings, and take our research further into multimodal AI, hardware and systems that act in the physical world. The more of the world our data reflects, the more of the world those systems can serve.


One million people have chosen to join Luel. Thank you for being part of what comes next.


Want to take part?[Join as a contributor](https://www.luel.ai/contribute) . Building something that needs data the internet does not have?[Tell us what you need](https://www.luel.ai/request) .
